name: al-Kalhabah
bio: Hubairah ibn 'Abd-Manaf, called al-Kalhabah, belonged to a subdivision of the tribe of Yarbu' ibn Handhalah, a branch of Tamim, and had settled at Zarud among the men of Malik ibn Handhalah.
Lyall gives the occasion of Ode II: the tribe of Malik was raided by men of Taghlib, and the poet pursued them on his mare 'Aradah, 'the Locust'. Ode III, in the same vein, praises the mare.

poems.title: Ode II: Yea, if thou escapest from her
poems.author: al-Kalhabah
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Hubairah son of 'Abd-Manaf, of 'Arin, called al-Kalhabah.
poems.text:
Yea, if thou escapest from her, O Hazimah son of Tariq, at least she has left thee bare of all things behind thy back !

The Crier of our tribe shouted — ' The enemy are upon you ' : that moment my mare had drunk the whole of a water-skin.

I called to Ka's — 'Bridle her quick!' for in sooth I came to dwell on the hill of Zarud for nought else but to render help at need.

The arrows that stuck in the sides of her neck and about her throat were like stalks of leeks pulled up from a level sandy plain.

Then lameness beset my Locust, and wrecked her reserve of speed, when already a finger's breadth only parted Hazimah from me.

I gave you my orders there where the failing sand-edge curves : but no authority rests with him who is disobeyed.

Yea, when a man faces not boldly the ugly things that come, the cords of quietness soon will snap, and his peace decay.

poems.title: Ode III: The Sons of Jusham son of
poems.author: al-Kalhabah
poems.note: Lyall's heading: The same, in praise of his mare 'the Locust'.
poems.text:
The Sons of Jusham son of Bakr ask me whether the Locust has a white blaze on her forehead, or is all of one colour.

She is the steed that dashed against them, on her back the wounded old warrior like a lion.

When her charge has taken her through their ranks, she returns to charge them again, and the spears hold her back so that she cannot move.

Three of her legs are like one another in having a white ring round the pastern, while one leg is all of one colour.

She is a bay, of no doubtful hue, but the colour of .sw/into which the hide to be dyed has been plunged a second time.
